entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Pharnaces II of Pontus was a king of the Bosporan Kingdom and Kingdom of Pontus from 63 BC until his death in 46 BCE. He was the youngest child of King Mithridates VI of Pontus and his first wife, Queen Laodice, who was also his sister. This made Pharnaces II the namesake of his late double great grandfather Pharnaces I of Pontus. After his father's defeat by the Romans in the Third Mithridatic War and death in 63 BC, the Romans annexed the Kingdom of Pontus.

Pharnaces II's reign was marked by the Bosporan Kingdom's continued struggles against Roman expansion. Despite his efforts to resist Roman rule, Pharnaces II's kingdom eventually fell to the Romans.

Pharnaces II's legacy is significant in the history of the region. His reign highlights the complex web of alliances and rivalries between the various kingdoms and empires of the ancient world. The Roman annexation of the Kingdom of Pontus marked a significant turning point in the region's history, setting the stage for the rise of the Roman Empire.

One of the most striking aspects of Pharnaces II's reign is the sheer scale of the Roman military's intervention in the region. The Roman army's victory in the Third Mithridatic War marked a significant milestone in the Roman Empire's expansion into the eastern Mediterranean.

Pharnaces II's story serves as a reminder of the complex and often fraught relationships between ancient kingdoms and empires. His reign offers a fascinating glimpse into the intricate web of alliances and rivalries that defined the ancient world.
